REWARD-TO-RISK, RECOMPUTED HERE FROM FINAL LEVELS, NOT COPIED FROM THE NOTES: TJX 2.27, FRO 2.45, CEG 2.75, HD 3.00, SLV 3.00, XLE 3.04, DHT 3.11, /MBTU6 3.25. HORIZON SKEW, STATED RATHER THAN CORRECTED: 8 swing, 2 long-term, 0 intraday. Three large retail prints land before the open today (TJX, TGT, LOW), so intraday catalysts genuinely existed — research had no differentiated view on any of them and declined to manufacture one. FOUR OF TEN ARE MARKED WAIT and are held out of performance tracking: XLE and FRO (do not chase the range high), SLV and CEG (accumulate only below a stated level). Six of ten are updates to positions already open rather than new risk. Total deployed capital if every level fills is 18%.

CONVICTION WAS CUT, NOT RAISED, BY TWO LATE PASSES. The falsification pass found an active Oman-mediated Hormuz reopening track that Iran's foreign minister calls 'very close' — evidence directly against the book's largest bet — cutting XLE 4->3, DHT 4->3 and FRO 3->2 with FRO's size halved to 1%. Separately, research caught that its own stated reason for preferring CEG was factually backwards: post-Calpine, Constellation has MORE Texas ERCOT exposure and is divesting PJM assets, so the Texas data-centre pause is its problem too. PRICES: every last_price is the 2026-08-18 16:00 ET close, fetched from finnhub at 06:33 ET into a pre-market session. That is a closed market, not a stale quote. /MBTU6 carries last_price null — the contract itself could not be quoted; BTC spot was 64,376 on coingecko at synthesis, against the 64,340 the entry level was set from.

SOURCES THAT FAILED, AND WHAT THAT COST: (1) Event contracts were a total loss — eleven Kalshi queries across inflation, Fed, rates, Iran, oil, gas, S&P, Bitcoin, GDP, shutdown and Powell returned zero markets or unpriced sports shards, so no implied probability was obtainable and no event idea was captured. That is a gap, not an absence of opportunity. (2) No live VIX, DXY, SPX, NDX, DJI, RUT, gold or WTI futures quotes — Yahoo returned HTTP 429 throughout and finnhub requires an index subscription. Index context in market_context comes from stooq ETF proxies; the macro read leans on FRED rates, which did resolve. (3) Robinhood's canonical futures-contract support article now 404s, so venue verification for /MBTU6 used Robinhood's 'before trading a futures contract' page plus secondary coverage; micro Bitcoin futures were confirmed offered. Robinhood offers NO interest-rate or Treasury futures, which is the binding constraint on today's report — the strongest macro read is the term-premium blowout at the long end and there is no direct way to trade it in this account, so it is expressed second-hand through the BCC exit, the LCII cancellation and the HD warning.

IDEAS DROPPED, AND WHY: ASC and STNG (product-tanker laggards, -10% and -9% off highs) were dropped purely on the 3-per-driver correlation cap, not on merit — Hormuz is already three deep with XLE, FRO and DHT. ZIM merger arb was rejected on arithmetic ($35 cash bid against 28.49, but R:R 0.69 versus a 2.0 floor) and UI on unverifiable consensus; both are real opportunities a reader may want despite these rules. No small caps were captured — the lane was hunted across fourteen names and everything failed liquidity, was a falling knife with no dated catalyst, or was correlated into the full Hormuz bucket.

ONE UNVERIFIED ASSERTION, FLAGGED BY RESEARCH ITSELF: the DHT counter-argument claims its fleet is older and its charter mix less spot-levered than Frontline's. That was not verified from a filing. It sits in the counter-argument, so if wrong it only made the call more cautious — but it should not be read as a sourced fact. Every price, ATR, moving average and range figure in the research log was fetched via market_data.py; none was estimated.

RED TEAM (separate pass, 07:05-07:2x ET, working from the validation blocks and re-reading sources rather than the report's own summaries).

FRO moved to the watchlist, on three grounds and none of them the geopolitics: it was the third position on the Hormuz driver and the only one adding new risk (XLE and DHT are existing lots being held); the 42.20 entry sits against a close 0.89% below the 150-day high of 43.89, verified from history, so the edge is already paid for; and the 52.00 target is 6.78 ATR away and 18.5% above the entire 150-day range with no support, resistance or valuation behind it — the validator flagged it and it is the number that makes 2.45:1 work. ONE MISSED EVENT, WHICH IS THE LARGEST FINDING. HD reported Q2 FY2026 before the open on 2026-08-18 — the same morning the long was opened at 340.00 — and the report never mentioned it, describing that session as 'a slow five-session grind' when it was a 330.69-344.54 earnings bar on 6.6m shares against a ~3m average. Against: HD beat, reaffirmed, and still closed red below both moving averages, so it is being priced on the 30-year rather than on its own numbers, and its company catalyst is spent. ONE PIECE OF EVIDENCE OVERSTATED, AGAINST THE BOOK'S OWN INTEREST. The research phase cut XLE and DHT from 4 to 3 on an 'Oman-mediated Hormuz reopening track' it called 'very close.' Re-reading the reporting, that is not what the sources say: Iran and Oman have agreed inbound and outbound routes and are finalising a shipping map, but Iran's foreign minister Araghchi said on 08-16 that reopening the strait 'is a separate issue. A correct call reached through a misread is still a misread, and the reader should not be trading the wrong reason.

NOT CUT, DELIBERATELY. TJX carries the thinnest ratio at 2.27 and is a binary held into a print inside two hours with an unenforceable stop — but it says all of that itself, it is a hold rather than a fresh entry, and the vendor calendar independently confirms the 08-19 bmo date at $1.20 EPS on $15.34B against the report's $1.19 on $15.17B. market_context.summary:
The tape is being driven by a term-premium blowout at the long end: the 30-year Treasury yield sits at its highest level in nearly two decades on persistent inflation risk, heavy government borrowing and debt issuance tied to the AI capex boom. This is a supply and term-premium story rather than a growth story, and it is repricing long-duration equity downward while bidding energy and hard assets. The 2-year at 4.19% is roughly 56bp above the 3.63% effective funds rate, so the market is pricing tightening, not cuts. On 2026-08-18 the Nasdaq fell 1.3% with the semiconductor gauge down 5.5% in a single session, while XLE rose 1.76% — its third straight day of relative strength and the only green sector.

The second dominant fact is the Strait of Hormuz, effectively closed at roughly 3 transits a day against about 130 pre-war, with Brent at $90.97 and WTI above $84. But that trade is more two-sided than it looks: a separate Oman-mediated shipping track is reportedly near agreement, with Iran's foreign minister calling a waterway-management deal 'very close.' The honest posture that falls out is to hold energy rather than add to it, cut the rate-sensitive cyclicals, and do the real buying in the AI-power de-rate — which is exactly the shape of today's report.

Retail earnings week is the entire catalyst calendar: LOW, TGT, TJX, ADI and EL all report before the open today, WMT tomorrow, NVDA on 08-26. The consumer, not semis, is the tradeable theme this week.

recommendations.thesis: TJX has de-rated 11.3% from its 170.00 range high to 150.85, closing below its 20-day (156.59) and 50-day (157.35) on eight sessions of selling into a print it has beaten four quarters running by an average of 8.8%. The position is already open and effectively flat at -0.4%; this is a hold decision, not a fresh entry, and the reward-to-risk of 2.27 describes the trade from here rather than the risk actually being taken this morning.
recommendations.counter_argument: The eight-session slide may be informed rather than random — the whole retail complex sold off ahead of LOW, TGT, TJX and WMT, and insiders sold $32.5M across nine transactions in six months with zero open-market purchases. If the sell-off is discounting a genuine comp deceleration, an EPS beat with soft traffic guidance still gets sold, which is the most common way this loses.

HD is less exposed to it, not immune. Layered on top is a same-morning event, LOW reporting before the open, that can gap HD straight through the 328.00 stop before any decision is possible.
recommendations.counter_argument: Holding the one housing name while exiting the other two is now evidenced rather than rationalised — HD reaffirmed guidance while LCI cut its shipment forecast roughly 10% — but the market has seen both facts and sold HD anyway. That is the strongest case against: if the rate thesis is right, repair and remodel decelerates too, just later, and a reaffirmed guide given on 08-18 does not incorporate a 30-year yield that made its high after the print. Fundamentals lagging price is the normal order of events at a turn.

catalyst.event: Data-centre electricity demand growing 26-27% in 2026 to 132GW from 104GW against a generation base that cannot be built at that speed — roughly 40% of announced AI data-centre projects are delayed by power infrastructure, not chip supply
catalyst.action: Accumulate below 248 only — do not pay 266.83. Build in thirds: first third under 248, second under 236, final third under 220. A two-to-three year hold; expect to add through drawdowns. Conviction cut 4->3 and size 4%->3% after finding an error in my own first pass, described in key_risk.

recommendations.thesis: The AI-power complex de-rated 23-40% (NRG -39%, TLN -29%, CEG -23%, VST -23%) on a Texas-specific setback — the state paused new data-centre projects, cutting forecast ERCOT load growth from 14% to 5.6%, and NRG cleared Houston power at $33/MWh against a $52 plan. The national demand curve did not move: Gartner has data-centre electricity consumption up 26% in 2026, hyperscalers guided to $635-670B of combined 2026 capex, and the binding constraint on ~40% of announced projects is power infrastructure rather than chips. Constellation owns the scarce asset — the largest US zero-emission nuclear fleet, which is what hyperscalers sign long-dated PPAs against, and the January 2026 Calpine deal added roughly 27GW and about $2B of annual free cash flow for a 55GW combined fleet.
recommendations.key_risk: Correcting my own first pass: I originally argued CEG was insulated because it is PJM-weighted rather than ERCOT-exposed. That is wrong. Constellation closed the $16.4B Calpine acquisition on 2026-01-07, which brought a largely natural-gas fleet with significant Texas ERCOT exposure, and it is simultaneously SELLING PJM generation assets to LS Power under a DOJ antitrust condition. So CEG is moving toward more Texas exposure and less PJM — the Texas pause is its problem too, not a risk it sidesteps. That removes the specific reason I preferred it to VST and NRG and is why conviction and size are cut. Invalidation stays fundamental: hyperscaler combined capex guided below roughly $500B for 2027, or PJM capacity clearing prices falling in two consecutive auctions.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that these stocks were priced for a scarcity rent regulators will not permit a generator to collect — power is politically administered, and the more valuable the electron is to a data centre the likelier a state PUC intervenes for retail ratepayers. Texas already demonstrated exactly this by pausing projects. CEG has also already bounced 10.4% in 30 days, so the easy part of the recovery is gone; and at 266.83 the reward-to-risk against a 205 bear case is 1.43, failing the 2.5 long-term floor outright — which is why this is accumulate-below-248 (R:R 2.75) and not a buy here.

recommendations.thesis: Silver peaked at $121/oz in January 2026 and now trades near $63, having erased more than half its all-time high in the sharpest correction in decades — but the correction was driven by positioning and a strong dollar, not by the supply picture, which is still in multi-year structural deficit against solar, EV and electronics demand. SLV at 57.44 sits above a flat 20-day (55.36) and 50-day (55.51), which is a base forming rather than a downtrend, and the debasement driver strengthened this week as the 30-year hit a two-decade high on government borrowing concerns.
recommendations.key_risk: Invalidation is fundamental, not a price level: if the structural deficit closes — two consecutive years of surplus in the Silver Institute balance, or solar silver-thrifting cutting grams-per-watt faster than installations grow — the thesis is dead regardless of price. The live danger is that the exact force that caused the crash is intensifying right now: high real rates and a firm dollar are what broke silver, and the 30-year at a two-decade high makes that worse before it makes it better.
recommendations.counter_argument: Catching a metal down 50% from a vertical blow-off is the classic way to be early and wrong for years — silver did precisely this after 1980 and after 2011, taking a decade to recover each time. Industrial demand is described as declining on higher energy costs, so the demand leg is currently working against the thesis, not for it. At spot 57.44 the reward-to-risk does not clear the 2.5 long-term floor at all, which is exactly why this is written as a wait-for-54 order rather than a buy.

watchlist.note: Cut by the red team. Three separate reasons, none of them the geopolitics. (1) Correlation: it is the third Hormuz-driver position and the only one adding NEW risk — XLE and DHT are existing lots being held, FRO was a fresh 1% entry on the identical ton-mile thesis, so the book was being asked to take the same bet a third time. (2) The edge is priced: entry 42.20 against a close of 43.50 that is 0.89% below the 150-day high of 43.89, verified from history. Buying the highest-beta name in a complex at its high is the worst place to be wrong, which the idea itself conceded. (3) The level is not real: the 52.00 target is 6.78 ATR away — the validator flagged it — and sits 18.5% above the entire 150-day range. There is no resistance, no prior trade and no valuation anchor at 52; it is the number that makes 2.45:1 work. Its own counter-argument (4.2x as a value trap, VLCC volumes at 12.3m bpd the weakest of the crisis, zero insider open-market buys) was stronger than its thesis, and a conviction-2 idea whose author argues the bear case better does not belong in the book.
watchlist.trigger: A pullback to the 20-day at 39.54 with VLCC volume — not just rates — turning back up, or room in the Hormuz bucket if XLE or DHT is closed. The 08-31 print is a real catalyst; it does not justify paying the range high three weeks early.
watchlist.demotion_reason: Third position on one driver, entry 0.89% off the 150-day high, target 6.78 ATR beyond any anchor.

watchlist.note: Rejected on arithmetic, and surfaced because a reader may want it despite the rule. A $35.00 cash bid against 28.49 is a 6.51 reward, but a realistic break case of 19-20 against a 15.50 unaffected price makes risk about 9.5 — R:R 0.69 versus a 2.0 swing floor. Merger arb is structurally high-probability and low-payoff and will always fail an R:R floor; the floor exists to reject ideas, so it was not re-drawn to make this pass.
